chunks: Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad, from ʿAlī ibn al-Ḥakam, from ʿAlī ibn Abī Ḥamzah, from Abū Baṣīr, who said:
I asked Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام about the saying of Allah, Mighty and Majestic:
“But whoever gives it in charity, then it is an expiation for him.”
He عليه السلام said: “It is expiated for him from his sins in proportion to what he has pardoned of a wound or other than it.”
He said: And I asked him about the saying of Allah, Mighty and Majestic:
“So whoever is pardoned anything by his brother, then there should be a follow-up in a fair manner and payment to him with excellence.”

He عليه السلام said: “It is the man who accepts the blood-money; then the claimant ought to deal gently with him and not make things hard for him, and the one from whom it is sought ought to pay it to him with excellence, so he should not delay him when he is able.”

key_terms.بِالْمَعْرُوفِ: in a fair and proper manner
key_terms.كَفَّارَةٌ: expiation for sins resulting from an act of pardon
key_terms.يَمْطُلْهُ: he delays payment despite being able

ai.seo_question: What do the Qur'anic verses about pardoning injury and accepting blood-money mean?
ai.summary: This hadith explains two Qur'anic verses concerning pardon and compensation in cases of injury and killing. It teaches that remitting one's right counts as expiation for sins, and that when blood-money is accepted, both the claimant and the debtor must act with fairness, gentleness, and ihsan.
